question: In a diabetic patient with medial arterial calcification, an ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI) of 1.2 reliably indicates normal arterial perfusion of the lower limb.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. Diabetic patients with medial arterial calcification have incompressible vessel walls, meaning the cuff pressure required to occlude flow is artificially high — giving a falsely elevated or normal-appearing ABPI despite significant ischaemia. Toe pressure or duplex Doppler is preferred in such patients.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Medial calcification renders the vessel wall incompressible, producing falsely elevated ABPI readings. An ABPI above 1.3 (or even 1.2 in high-suspicion diabetics) should be treated as unreliable, and toe pressures or duplex ultrasound should be used instead.
